newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Metrobank says no loan woes with San Carlos.
newsitem.headline: Metrobank says no loan woes with San Carlos.

text.p: Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co (Metrobank) denied rumours on Wednesday that one of its debtors, San Carlos Milling Co, was experiencing financial difficulties.

"The rumour is not true. The account is not experiencing any cash flow problem, no problem at all. The account is current and it is a well-managed account," said Alfredo Javellana, Metrobank comptroller.
Javellana said Metrobank has 500 million pesos in loans with San Carlos secured by its sugar mill valued at 1.4 billion pesos.
Another 500 million pesos in letters of credit are also secured by a property in the financial district of Makati worth 450 million pesos.

"My analysis is that they (San Carlos) tend to maximise credit terms when it comes to payment...and this may probably have been overheard as a delay in payment. But they are not delayed," said Javellana.
Traders said the rumour caused Metrobank's share price to tumble 3.47 percent to close at 555 pesos. It was the most heavily traded stock of the day.
An official of San Carlos also denied talk that the firm was facing financial difficulties due to its huge inventory of imported sugar.
Another sugar miller, Victorias Milling Corp, created a stir in recent months when it sought a 90-day moratorium on the principal payment of its 4.42 billion peso loans.
